transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (CobaltWorks SRE), Maya (Platform), Jordan (Security), Liam (infra)

Summary (auto): Brief latency tail increase post-kernel upgrade; routing fallback exercised twice last week; security asks around KMS and audit logs; agreed on telemetry sweep and canary rehearsal.

[00:00] Alex (AE): okay, uh thanks everyone for joining, let's run through the agenda. Priya and I will quick recap of what we saw in the last 72 hours, then Sam/Maya you can walk through the handoff and failures you observed.
[00:22] Priya (SE): yeah, thanks. So short version, after the 1.14 kernel bump we saw the 99th latency jump about 20-30% on long context walks, most pronounced when requests hit the fallback route. Might be connection churn, maybe MTU-related packet fragmentation, still investigating.
[00:45] Sam (SRE): right, we saw that at 02:14 UTC on Friday - lots of half-handshakes where the PSK handshake failed and connection retried to a second path. I attached traces in the ticket but i'll share a pcap after this.
[01:10] Maya (Platform): there's also a pattern where bigger payloads get fragmented across the private bridge, and if the second path is the fallback it's slower; sometimes session affinity drops and requests go cold.
[01:38] Priya (SE): mhm, session affinity and KV cache warming are two interacting things here — if we drop KV cache we re-emit prefix tokens which pushes the tail. We have an experimental tweak to keep the cache pinned for a short TTL on warm sessions. We'll include that in the sweep.
[02:05] Jordan (Security): quick security check — for any change that touches keying/handshake we need KMS integration notes and an audit log retention plan. Our compliance team requires explicit log retention for 12 months.
[02:28] Alex (AE): absolutely, we'll send the security bundle. Priya, can you note telemetry fields Jordan needs?
[02:36] Priya (SE): yes, Jordan — we'd capture handshake result, path ID, MTU observed, connection reset count, and KV cache miss rate. I'll add a tlog field for the canary.
[03:00] Liam (infra): there's also an MTU mismatch between our edge and the private bridge, we've been seeing 1460 vs 9000 occasionally; that causes fragmentation and some vendor switches drop fragmented packets.
[03:30] Priya (SE): that would explain the fragmentation. Two things we can do: one, enforce MSS clamping at the bridge; two, fall back to a path that reports jumbo enabled. We'll test both in the sweep.
[04:00] Sam (SRE): question — when you say fallback path, what are the selection heuristics? Last week it seemed random.
[04:15] Priya (SE): selection is first-by-policy: region > latency_slo > cost_tier. If region matches and latency is within threshold it keeps primary, otherwise we pick the next compatible model+path. But there is a slight race if the primary is flapping and the control plane reconciles slowly. We're tuning the debounce window.
[04:48] Alex (AE): and to be clear, the debounce change won't change SLA, it just reduces thrash during transient failures.
[05:05] Maya (Platform): okay, on Friday we had two fallback events, one that escalated to the second region and increased tail lat by 400ms. Our app times out at 600ms for certain flows so that impacted user experience for a small sample.
[05:30] Priya (SE): noted. We'll run a sweep that simulates your timeout profile — 50% short flows, 50% 4k context long flows — to reproduce.
[05:52] Sam (SRE): regarding kernel: are there known sysctl params or patch versions that are recommended? We can roll back but want to avoid churn.
[06:05] Priya (SE): the 1.14 contained a tcp retransmit behavior change that made short-lived connections more sensitive to PMTU; we've got a recommended sysctl set to relax RTO and enable path MTU probing timeout extension. We'll include the exact sysctl snippet in the runbook.
[06:35] Jordan (Security): also want to confirm whether keys are held in customer KMS or Redwood-managed. For on-prem we prefer customer KMS/HSM.
[06:48] Alex (AE): if you want customer-managed KMS we support HSM integrations; that will be listed as an enterprise add-on. We'll send options.
[07:05] Maya (Platform): what about audit logs and retention? We need token-level call traces for 90 days accessible, and aggregated telemetry for 12 months.
[07:20] Priya (SE): we can ship token-level traces for 90d; for aggregated we can stream to your S3 with lifecycle policies for 12 months. Jordan, we'll include the S3 log schema.
[07:40] Sam (SRE): one more operational piece: our netops wants a dry-run to simulate a 10% traffic shift to fallback to validate downstream caches. Can Redwood run at scale?
[07:55] Priya (SE): yes we can. We'll run a canary that ramps to 10% for 30 minutes, then 30% for 10 min, with a rollback window. That will validate caches and KV warming.
[08:20] Alex (AE): and pricing for that burst? We'll note it in the updated pricing doc — burst reserved vs on-demand fallback cost.
[08:33] Maya (Platform): okay thanks. On telemetry I noticed two missing labels in the dashboard during the last incident — path_id and handshake_result were empty for ~12% of events.
[08:48] Priya (SE): that sounds like a race where the control-plane didn't tag early telemetry; we'll add an early tag emission to the SDK so path_id is set at connect time. That will make the dashboard more reliable.
[09:10] Sam (SRE): sending the pcap now to the ticket; it has three failed SYNs then a successful connect on alternate path. Looks like MSS issue.
[09:28] Alex (AE): thanks. We'll triage and priya will run the sweep.
[09:35] Speaker 1: [unintelligible]
[09:40] Priya (SE): small nit — we'll also test a patch that pins KV cache for 30s on reconnect to reduce cold tails; that has low risk.
[10:01] Jordan (Security): for KMS, do you have an implementation guide for rotating keys? We have strict rotation policies and want to ensure Redwood-managed doesn't break ops.
[10:15] Alex (AE): rotation is supported; we'll share the rotation diagram — customer rotation hooks -> Redwood verifier -> revocation propagation. We'll include time-to-revoke guarantees.
[10:36] Maya (Platform): timeline question — when can we expect the sweep and the runbook?
[10:45] Priya (SE): i'll run the sweep Tues-Wed, upload CSV and filtered telemetry dashboard by Thursday. The runbook draft for the rehearsed canary will be ready by Friday.
[11:02] Sam (SRE): fine. Also, can you scope a light-weight on-prem package if we want an air-gapped control plane? Not full on-prem but hybrid.
[11:18] Alex (AE): we have a hybrid option with customer control-plane and Redwood-managed runtime; that's an enterprise option — we can put together rough SOW and pricing.
[11:33] Priya (SE): another technical note: we recommend enabling prefix caching warmup in the runtime for your long context calls; that'll reduce token regen and drop tail. We'll include the config toggle.
[11:55] Maya (Platform): any blockers from Redwood side for the rehearsal?
[12:01] Priya (SE): none — just need Sam to provide pcap and netops to reserve the rehearsal window. Also we need the PSK exchange details 24h before rehearsal.
[12:18] Sam (SRE): noted. We'll get PSK to your secure share and set up a test route.
[12:28] Alex (AE): cool. Let's recap next steps.
[12:33] Alex (AE): Priya runs the sweep and adds the early path_id tag. Alex sends pricing + security docs. Sam provides pcap and schedules rehearsal. Maya schedules netops slot. Jordan confirms KMS requirements.
[12:55] Maya (Platform): sounds good. Do we want to lock a target date for the rehearsal now?
[13:02] Alex (AE): how does 2026-12-20 look for everyone?
[13:08] Maya (Platform): that works for netops.
[13:12] Sam (SRE): works for SRE.
[13:16] Jordan (Security): tentative yes, pending doc review.
[13:22] Alex (AE): great, we'll treat 2026-12-20 as the rehearsal target, final go/no-go 48h prior.
[13:30] Priya (SE): i'll also include the sysctl snippet for the 1.14 behavior and the TTL pin for KV cache.
[13:42] Speaker 2: [muffled agreement]
[13:50] Alex (AE): ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items in the ticket and calendar invite for the rehearsal.
[14:00] Meeting end.

Attachments referenced: https://redwood.app/decks/cobaltworks-kernel-1.14-readout.pdf, ticket#CWB-872, shared drive link: drive.company/cobaltworks/poc-telemetry (redacted)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label confusion around 09:35 and 13:42, some technical terms spelled phonetically (PSK/handshake sometimes as P-S-K), overall medium-quality auto-transcription with domain-specific words occasionally mistranscribed.
